belongs_to: Sameeksha's room problem: 'The main room of the house is 12 ft by 16 ft ... What size tiles should she buy?' (page 2 later says 'rough diagrams like the one shown on the previous page')
description: A hand-drawn rectangle (the room), long side horizontal, with no tiles, grid or fill inside. Top: a double-headed horizontal arrow running the full width above the top side, with the label '16 ft' written in the middle of the arrow (arrowheads at both ends: left and right). Right: a double-headed vertical arrow just to the right of the right side, the same height as the rectangle, with the label '12 ft' in the middle (arrowheads at top and bottom). Right-angle (small square) marks are drawn inside THREE corners only: top-left, top-right and bottom-left; the bottom-right corner has no mark. Only the two measurements 16 ft and 12 ft are written; no tile size or tile count is shown.

belongs_to: 'Procedure for Prime Factorisation - Can you see what is happening below?' (left of the two figures, for 105)
description: Vertical factor tree for 105 with 2 circled numbers. Top circle: 105. A short vertical line goes down from it to a second circle: 35. A short vertical line goes down from 35 to the plain (uncircled) number 7 at the bottom. To the left of each circle a prime label is joined to the circle by a short horizontal line: '3' joined to the 105 circle, '5' joined to the 35 circle. So left column reads 3, 5 and the bottom reads 7. No colours, no loop.

belongs_to: 'Procedure for Prime Factorisation - Can you see what is happening below?' (right of the two figures, for 30)

belongs_to: 'We collect the prime factors along the left and the one at the bottom. We then construct the prime factorisation as shown in the figure.' (105)
description: The 105 factor tree again, at the right edge of page 50: circle 105 on top, vertical line down to circle 35, vertical line down to the plain number 7. Left labels joined by horizontal lines: '3' to the 105 circle, '5' to the 35 circle. Added in this version: one blue closed curve (a long curved banana/loop shape) that starts around the '3' at the top left, runs down the left side past the '5', and ends in a pointed loop around the '7' at the bottom; it encloses the three prime labels 3, 5 and 7 (the horizontal line of the 5 and the vertical line to the 7 cross/touch the curve). Caption printed under the figure: '105 = 3 × 5 × 7'.

belongs_to: 'the circles are usually left out and the steps are carried out in this format' (division method for 105, left of the two ladders)

Reads: 3 | 105, 5 | 35, then 7. Plain black text, grey rules, no colour or loop.

belongs_to: 'the circles are usually left out and the steps are carried out in this format' (division method for 30, right of the 105 ladder)

belongs_to: 'Find the factors of 225 using prime factorisation.' (ladder printed at the right of the text)
description: Division-method ladder for 225 with 4 divisor rows and a last quotient 1. Left column of divisors from top to bottom: 5, 5, 3, 3. Rows (each stepped one place to the right of the previous one, each with a horizontal line under its number): '5 | 225', '5 | 45', '3 | 9', '3 | 3'. Below the last row the quotient '1' stands alone. Plain black text, grey rules, no colour. The text gives 225 = 5 × 5 × 3 × 3.

belongs_to: Example 1: 'Find the common factors, and the HCF of 45 and 75' (45 = 3 × 3 × 5 and 75 = 3 × 5 × 5; 'common factors should be subparts of both the factorisations. Can you write them down?')
description: Three blocks stacked vertically, each block = two rows of factors (upper row is 45 = 3 × 3 × 5, lower row is 75 = 3 × 5 × 5, the '45 =' / '75 =' labels are not printed) and a plain label to the right of the block. Circled factors (red digit inside a black circle) show the matched common subpart. Block 1, label '3': upper row ③ × 3 × 5, lower row ③ × 5 × 5 (first 3 circled in both rows). Block 2, label '5': upper row 3 × 3 × ⑤, lower row 3 × 5 × ⑤ (last 5 circled in both rows). Block 3, label '3 × 5': upper row 3 × ③ × ⑤ (second 3 and the 5 circled), lower row ③ × ⑤ × 5 (first 3 and second factor 5 circled; the last 5 plain). Total circles: 2 + 2 + 4 = 8. Rows are not boxed or joined by lines.

belongs_to: Example 2: 'Find the common factors, and the HCF of 112 and 84' (112 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 7, 84 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7; 'Finding the common subparts, we get')
description: Five blocks stacked vertically, each = two rows (upper row is 112 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 7, lower row is 84 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7; the '112 =' / '84 =' labels are not printed) with a plain label to the right. Circled factors are red digits in black circles. Block 1, label '2': upper ② × 2 × 2 × 2 × 7, lower ② × 2 × 3 × 7. Block 2, label '7': upper 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × ⑦, lower 2 × 2 × 3 × ⑦. Block 3, label '2 × 2': upper 2 × ② × ② × 2 × 7 (2nd and 3rd 2 circled), lower ② × ② × 3 × 7 (1st and 2nd 2 circled). Block 4, label '2 × 7': upper ② × 2 × 2 × 2 × ⑦ (1st 2 and the 7 circled), lower 2 × ② × 3 × ⑦ (2nd 2 and the 7 circled). Block 5, label '2 × 2 × 7': upper ② × ② × 2 × 2 × ⑦ (1st, 2nd 2 and 7 circled), lower ② × ② × 3 × ⑦ (1st, 2nd 2 and 7 circled). Circle counts per block: 2, 2, 4, 4, 6 (total 18).

belongs_to: Example 4: 'Find the HCF of 30 and 72' - 'This has been carried out below' (largest common subpart, one 2 and one 3)
description: Two rows with a result line. Row 1: '30 = [2] × [3] × 5'. Row 2: '72 = [2] × 2 × 2 × [3] × 3'. The 2 and the 3 are red digits in blue rounded boxes. Box 1: one tall blue box around the first 2 of row 1 and the first 2 of row 2 (both rows, same column). Box 2: a blue boxed '3' in row 1 (the 3 of 30) joined by a blue L-shaped outline running right along the gap between the rows to a blue boxed '3' in row 2 (the first 3 of 72, the 4th factor; the last 3 of 72 stays plain). Under them: 'HCF = 2 × 3 = 6'. The 5 in 30 and the other 2s and the second 3 in 72 are black and unboxed.

belongs_to: Example 5: 'Find the HCF of 225 and 750' - 'the largest common subpart should contain two 5s' (figure at the right of the text)
description: Two rows with a result line. Row 1: '225 = 3 × [3] × [5] × [5]'. Row 2: '750 = 2 × [3] × [5] × [5] × 5'. Three tall blue rounded boxes, each spanning both rows in one column: box 1 around the red 3 (2nd factor of 225, 2nd factor of 750), box 2 around a green 5 (3rd factor in both rows), box 3 around a green 5 (4th factor in both rows). The leading 3 of 225, the leading 2 of 750 and the last 5 of 750 are black and unboxed. Result line: 'HCF = 3 × 5 × 5 = 75', with the 3 in red and both 5s in green. Colours: 3 red, 5s green.

belongs_to: 'Anshu and Guna make torans out of strips of cloth. Multiple strips are placed one next to another to make a toran. Anshu uses strips of length 6 cm and Guna uses strips of 8 cm.'
description: Colour illustration (scene art) of two boys sitting on the floor, Anshu on the left (blue shirt) and Guna on the right (green shirt), each laying cloth strips end to end in a row. Anshu's row uses pink strips with a white pattern, Guna's row uses tan/beige strips; each boy holds one more strip in his hand. The two rows run diagonally down to the right and are not drawn to scale; no lengths, numbers or labels are written on the strips.
unclear: Exact number of strips in each row is not clear (about 4-5 pink, about 3 tan, plus one in each hand) and no length is printed, so it shows the idea of strips placed side by side, not data; probably decoration. A second picture on the same page (a photograph of gajak sweet in a tray) is a plain photograph that no question works on, so it is not listed.

belongs_to: 'What happens to the HCF of two numbers if both numbers are doubled?' - 'consider the numbers 270 and 50' (HCF = 2 × 5 = 10)
description: Two rows with a result line. Row 1: '270 = [2] × 3 × 3 × 3 × [5]'. Row 2: '50 = [2] × 5 × [5]'. The 2 is a red digit in a tall blue rounded box spanning both rows (first factor of both). The last 5 of 270 is a green digit in a blue box; the second 5 of 50 is a green digit in a blue box; the two boxes are joined by a blue L-shaped outline running along the gap between the rows (the boxed 5 of 50 sits under the left end of the connector, the boxed 5 of 270 at its right end). The first 5 of 50 and the three 3s are black and unboxed. Under them: 'HCF = 2 × 5 = 10'.

belongs_to: 'Let us double these numbers to get 540 and 100' (HCF = 2 × 2 × 5 = 20)
description: Two rows with a result line, printed under the 270/50 figure. Row 1: '540 = [2] × [2] × 3 × 3 × 3 × [5]'. Row 2: '100 = [2] × [2] × 5 × [5]'. The two 2s are red digits, each in its own tall blue rounded box spanning both rows (2 boxes). The last 5 of 540 and the last 5 of 100 are green digits in blue boxes joined by a blue L-shaped outline along the gap between the rows (same shape as in the 270/50 figure). The first 5 of 100 and the three 3s are black and unboxed. Under them: 'HCF = 2 × 2 × 5 =20.'

belongs_to: 'Consider the following two multiples of 14 - 14 × 6, 14 × 9. What is their HCF?' (HCF = 14 × 3 = 42)
description: Two rows with a result line. Row 1: '14 × 6 = 2 × 7 × 2 × [3]'. Row 2: '14 × 9 = 2 × 7 × 3 × [3]'. In each row the red '2 × 7' has a red curly brace under it with the red label '14' beneath. One large blue rounded box encloses the red '2 × 7' and its '14' labels in BOTH rows (one tall box over both rows). A second, narrow blue rounded box encloses the green 3 of row 1 and the green 3 of row 2 together (one tall box over both rows, at the right end). The plain '2' in row 1 and the plain '3' in row 2 (before the green 3) are black and unboxed. Under them: 'HCF = 14 × 3 = 42.'

belongs_to: 'Find the HCF in the following cases' - left ladder, 300 and 150 (HCF = 2 × 5 × 5 × 3)
description: Two-number division ladder with 4 divisor rows and a last pair. Left column of divisors from top: 2, 5, 5, 3. Rows (stepped to the right, each with a horizontal line under the pair): '2 | 300, 150', '5 | 150, 75', '5 | 30, 15', '3 | 6, 3'. Below the last row the pair '2, 1' stands alone. One blue closed oval (tall, slightly slanted) encloses only the four divisors 2, 5, 5, 3 in the left column. Caption below: 'HCF = 2 × 5 × 5 × 3'.

belongs_to: 'Find the HCF in the following cases' - right ladder, 630 and 770 (HCF = 2 × 5 × 7)
description: Two-number division ladder with 3 divisor rows and a last pair, printed to the right of the 300/150 ladder. Left column of divisors from top: 2, 5, 7. Rows: '2 | 630, 770', '5 | 315, 385', '7 | 63, 77' (each stepped to the right with a horizontal line under the pair). Below the last row the pair '9, 11' stands alone. One blue closed oval encloses only the three divisors 2, 5, 7. Caption below: 'HCF = 2 × 5 × 7'.

belongs_to: 'This procedure not only gives the HCF but can also be used to find the LCM! Can you see how?' - left ladder, 300 and 150 (LCM = 2 × 5 × 5 × 3 × 2 × 1)
description: The 300/150 ladder drawn again, with one more row: left divisors from top 2, 5, 5, 3; rows '2 | 300, 150', '5 | 150, 75', '5 | 30, 15', '3 | 6, 3'; last pair '2, 1' below. This time ONE long blue curved loop encloses the four divisors 2, 5, 5, 3 in the left column, then sweeps down and round to the right, ending in a rounded end around the last pair '2, 1' (it passes under/through the '6, 3' row). So the marked numbers are 2, 5, 5, 3, 2, 1. Caption below: 'LCM = 2 × 5 × 5 × 3 × 2 × 1'.

belongs_to: 'Can be used to find the LCM' - right ladder, 630 and 770 (LCM = 2 × 5 × 7 × 3 × 3 × 11)
description: The 630/770 ladder with one more row than the HCF version: left divisors from top 2, 5, 7, 3; rows '2 | 630, 770', '5 | 315, 385', '7 | 63, 77', '3 | 9, 11'; last pair '3, 11' below. ONE long blue curved loop encloses the four divisors 2, 5, 7, 3, sweeps down and round to the right and ends in a rounded end around the last pair '3, 11'. So the marked numbers are 2, 5, 7, 3, 3, 11. Caption below: 'LCM = 2 × 5 × 7 × 3 × 3 × 11'.

belongs_to: Guna says 'I found a better way ... For the numbers 300 and 150, I can first directly divide both numbers by 50. The HCF will be 50 × 3.' (LCM 50 × 3 × 2 × 1 on the next page)

Plain black text, grey rules, no colour or loop.
